players.name: Payton Pritchard
players.outlook: Pritchard's minutes and production have increased in each of the last three seasons, peaking with his rounded 17 PPG, 5 APG, 4 RPG and 3 3PG last season. His role was expanded last season by the injury to Jayson Tatum, and he is likely to maintain that elevated level this season after the offseason trade of Jaylen Brown. Payton is an outstanding 3-point shooter and solid playmaker that the Celtics will rely on again this season, giving him top-50 fantasy upside in category leagues.

players.name: Jrue Holiday
players.outlook: Holiday enters his second season in Portland after averaging 16.3 PPG, 6.1 APG and 4.6 RPG in 29.4 MPG across 53 appearances. He remained a productive two-way guard. The concern is playing time in a crowded backcourt that now includes Damian Lillard, Ja Morant and Scoot Henderson. Holiday’s ability to contribute assists, threes and steals should keep him fantasy relevant, but a reduced role would lower his ceiling. He’s best viewed as a waiver wire option.

players.name: Peyton Watson
players.outlook: Watson arrives in Cleveland after a breakout season in Denver. He averaged career highs of 14.6 PPG, 4.9 RPG and 1.1 BPG while shooting 41.1% from beyond the arc, but his upside really showed when Nikola Jokic was out. Watson averaged 22.1 PPG, 5.8 RPG and 2.3 triples per game. A hamstring injury ended his season. With starter-level minutes expected in Cleveland, Watson is an intriguing late-round target with room to take another statistical jump.

players.name: Jeremiah Fears
players.outlook: Fears enters his second season with the Pelicans looking to turn flashes from a solid rookie year into a bigger role. He averaged 14.3 PPG, 3.7 RPG, 3.4 APG and 1.2 SPG while playing all 82 games, but shot just 33.0% from beyond the arc and struggled defensively. Fears’ playmaking improved as the season went on, and another step there could push him toward 17.0 PPG and 5.0 APG. The downside is that defensive issues could keep him from a full-time starting role. Fears is worth taking a chance on late in fantasy drafts.

players.name: Mitchell Robinson
players.outlook: Robinson is now with the Celtics after averaging 5.7 PPG, 8.8 RPG and 1.2 BPG in just 19.6 MPG for the Knicks last season. He also grabbed 4.2 offensive RPG, second most in the league, while shooting 72.3% from the field. Robinson can provide rebounds, blocks and a high field goal percentage, but he’ll compete with Neemias Queta for center minutes and remains a poor free throw shooter. Durability is another concern despite playing 60 games last season. He’s best viewed as a waiver wire option for managers looking for rebounds and blocks.

players.name: Quentin Grimes
players.outlook: Grimes arrives in Los Angeles after averaging 13.4 PPG, 3.6 RPG and 3.3 APG in 29.4 MPG for Philadelphia last season. He is expected to have a chance to start alongside Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves, which should create plenty of open looks. His usage could decline, but he’s worth taking a flier late in drafts for managers looking for points and threes.

players.name: Neemias Queta
players.outlook: Queta is coming off of a breakout season in which he averaged 10.2 PPG, 8.4 RPG and 1.3 BPG in 25.3 MPG while shooting 65.3% from the field. He started 75 of 76 games and emerged as a very good rim protector for Boston. The addition of Mitchell Robinson creates some uncertainty around his playing time, but Queta’s rebounds, blocks and high field goal percentage add to his fantasy appeal. His outlook will depend largely on how Boston divides the center minutes, making him better suited for the waiver wire outside of deeper leagues.

players.name: Egor Demin
players.outlook: Demin enters his second season after averaging 10.3 PPG, 3.2 RPG and 3.3 APG while shooting 38.5% from beyond the arc as a rookie. He was even better on catch-and-shoot attempts, hitting 40.5%, and showed more ability to attack the rim and create off the dribble during Summer League. With Mikel Brown Jr. and Julius Randle handling more of the offense, Demin should get a ton of opportunities off the ball. Plantar fasciitis remains a concern, but he’s a player fantasy managers should take a late round flier on if his scoring and playmaking continue to develop.

players.name: Scoot Henderson
players.outlook: Henderson’s role this season is uncertain role after averaging 14.2 PPG, 3.7 APG and 2.7 RPG in 24.9 MPG last season. He flashed his upside in the playoffs, including games of 31 and 21 points against San Antonio. The concern is playing time after Portland added Ja Morant to an already crowded backcourt. Henderson still has scoring and playmaking upside, but consistent minutes could be difficult to find.

players.name: Saddiq Bey
players.outlook: Bey recently signed a three-year extension with the Pelicans, but his role could change after New Orleans added Bennedict Mathurin and gets Dejounte Murray back. Bey averaged a career-high 17.7 PPG, 5.6 RPG, and 2.1 triples in 72 games last season, including 64 starts. He was even better after the All-Star break, averaging 20.0 PPG while shooting 40% from three. The concern is that a deeper rotation could reduce his minutes and usage. Bey is still worth a flier, especially if he remains a starter.

players.name: Draymond Green
players.outlook: Green averaged 8.4 PPG, 5.5 RPG and 5.5 APG in 27.5 MPG across 68 appearances. He also made 1.5 triples per game, though Green shot just 32.6% from deep. Steve Kerr wants Green taking more 3-pointers while also cutting down on turnovers after he averaged 2.7 per game last season. Green’s assists, rebounds and defensive stats still provide fantasy value, but his limited scoring keeps him more of a waiver wire option.

players.name: Daniel Gafford
players.outlook: Daniel Gafford enters the season looking to bounce back after ankle issues limited him to 55 games last season. He averaged 9.5 PPG, 6.9 RPG and 1.3 BPG in just 21.7 MPG while shooting 65.5% from the field. Gafford remains a good source of rebounds, blocks and elite field-goal efficiency, but his fantasy value will depend heavily on his playing time alongside Dereck Lively II. He’s best viewed as a waiver wire option, with considerably more upside if Lively misses time.

players.name: Malik Monk
players.outlook: Monk’s role in the rotation is uncertain after averaging 12.5 PPG and 3.0 APG in 22.0 MPG last season. He remained an effective perimeter scorer, shooting 39.5% from beyond the arc and 87.9% from the line, but appeared in only 62 games and made just three starts. Sacramento’s crowded backcourt could make consistent minutes difficult to come by. Monk can still provide scoring, threes and assists when given enough playing time, but he’s best viewed as a waiver-wire option in standard leagues.

players.name: Jakob Poeltl
players.outlook: Poeltl enters this season as the Raptors starting center after back issues limited him to 46 games last season. The early news is encouraging, with the Raptors saying he is moving well and looks good ahead of training camp. At his best, Poeltl is a steady source of rebounds, efficient scoring and defensive stats, as he averaged 14.5 PPG and 9.6 RPG while shooting 62.7% from the field in 2024-25. The concern is durability after last year’s back problems. Poeltl is worth a late-round pick in deeper leagues if his health holds up.

players.name: Collin Sexton
players.outlook: Collin Sexton enters this season as a key scoring option off the Lakers’ bench after averaging 15.4 PPG and 3.3 APG in just 23.7 MPG last season. He shot 48.5% from the field and 40.1% from three, including 44.5% on catch-and-shoot attempts. Sexton can create off the dribble, attack the rim and provide secondary playmaking, but a reserve role behind Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves limits his ceiling. He’s a source of points and triples, but is most likely a waiver wire add unless you are in a deeper league.

players.name: Jaime Jaquez Jr.
players.outlook: Jaquez Jr. arrives in Milwaukee as part of the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade, and he could see a larger role than he had in Miami. Jaquez averaged 15.4 PPG, 5.0 RPG and 4.7 APG last season while finishing second in Sixth Man of the Year voting. He can score inside, rebound and create for teammates, but his 3-point shooting remains the biggest concern after hitting 31.7% last season. If Jaquez’s minutes and usage increase, he has breakout potential.

players.name: Nikola Vucevic
players.outlook: Vucevic was a metronome of double-double production for 13 seasons, averaging a rounded 18 points and 11 rebounds from 2012-13 through 2024-25. Last season, he was traded to the Celtics midseason and saw his minutes and production dip precipitously. Some was due to performance and some to injury, but he was not fantasy viable with the Celtics. This offseason he returned to the Magic and is expected to compete with Wendell Carter Jr. for minutes. He may not get enough time to produce to his typical levels, but if for any reason he gets starter minutes again you can almost pencil his double-doub

players.name: Dillon Brooks
players.outlook: Brooks is coming off of the best season of his career. He averaged a career-high 20.2 PPG and 3.6 RPG while making 2.3 threes per game in his first season with the Suns. Brooks was even better in the playoffs, averaging 26.0 PPG and 6.0 RPG across four games against Oklahoma City. Brooks should remain an important part of the Suns’ rotation, but the return of Jalen Green and addition of Miles Bridges could reduce his scoring opportunities. He’s worth a flier at the end of drafts for managers looking for points, threes and steals.

players.name: Brook Lopez
players.outlook: Lopez could open the season as the Clippers’ projected starting center with Yanic Konan Niederhauser recovering from a Lisfranc injury and little proven depth behind him. Lopez averaged 8.5 PPG and 3.6 RPG in 75 games last season, but his role could grow with Los Angeles thin in the frontcourt. The concern is obvious at age 38, especially after an uneven 2025-26 season. Still, the minutes should be there if he stays healthy. Lopez is worth a flier for managers looking for threes and blocks.

players.name: Reed Sheppard
players.outlook: Sheppard got major minutes in Year 2, in part due to the injury absence of Fred VanVleet. Sheppard capitalized on those minutes to prove himself a plus shooter-scorer with enough playmaking, rebounding and defense to post positive peripheral numbers. However, VanVleet returns this season and the Rockets brought in Marcus Smart as well. Sheppard still has a key role for the team as a shooter and scorer off the bench, but his fantasy upside may be capped by role and minutes competition.

players.name: John Collins
players.outlook: Collins joined the Pistons this offseason and slots in to be one of their main scoring options in the frontcourt. He has averaged 19 or more points per game three times in his career, including two seasons ago with the Jazz. He excels at playing off an elite point guard, and Cade Cunningham should get him easy looks both at the rim and behind the arc. Collins is a top-100 fantasy prospect, but if he plays to his full capabilities he has top-50 upside in points leagues.

players.name: Aaron Gordon
players.outlook: Gordon enters this season looking to stay healthy after injuries limited him to just 36 games last season. He averaged 16.2 PPG, 5.8 RPG and 2.7 APG while shooting 49.7% from the field. Gordon can provide efficient scoring, rebounds and some three-point production, but durability has become a concern after he played only 51 games the previous season. He’s best viewed as a late-round bench stash, with his value tied closely to how many games he can stay on the floor.

players.name: Jerami Grant
players.outlook: Grant arrives in Memphis after averaging 18.6 PPG, 3.5 RPG and 2.1 APG while shooting 45.3% from the field with the Blazers last season. He remains a useful source of scoring and threes, but his modest rebounding and assist numbers limit his overall fantasy ceiling. Grant’s role could also fluctuate as the Grizzlies gives significant opportunities to young players like Cameron Boozer and Cedric Coward. He’s best viewed as a waiver wire option in standard leagues.
